// Build-A-Player College Football defensive linemen: generated by scripts/cfb/build-dls.mjs (ESPN feeds and PFF pages
// pulled 2026-11-25). Do not hand-edit rows; change the inputs (the build's dl/picks.json and dl/hand.json) and re-run.
// Read with data/cfb-players.js (the same row shape and the same 0-11 college scale) and data/dls.js (the NFL traits).
//
// ── Who is here ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Every 2026 FBS team (138): EDGE1, EDGE2 and DT1. {{COUNT}} rows. subpos 'edge' | 'dt'; espnPos is ESPN's roster position.
// Who plays: ESPN's rosters (DE / DT / NT / DL / EDGE, plus any LB PFF charts as an edge defender), lined up where PFF's
// 2026 team grade pages put him (ED = edge, DI = inside; a 'DI' under 265 lb is the end of an odd front, an edge here),
// with the NFL file's rule on top: 285 lb and up plays inside.
// The two edges and the tackle are the men with the most 2026 snaps at the spot (PFF's snap counts, every team charted;
// ESPN's box-score games and tackles + PD weighted to the latest four games break ties). When two tackles both play
// every down (snaps within 15%), DT1 is the better graded. Both edges start, so EDGE1 is the better graded of the two
// (depth 1) and EDGE2 the other (depth 2). A three-down front with one charted edge (Army) takes its lightest regular
// end under 285 lb as EDGE2.
// Checked against every team's latest box scores (Week 13 games through Nov 24): a man is treated as out (hurt or
// benched) and the next man plays when he has no box-score line in his team's last two games AND ESPN's games-played
// count also has him missing two (a lineman can play a quiet game without a stat), unless the injury check below kept
// him because he is expected back this season (the Simmons rule). Every man the check touched, and the season-ending
// injuries, are named here:
{{PICKS}}
// Bio (number, height, weight, class) and photo: ESPN. espn = the ESPN athlete id. year: ESPN's roster class, with RS-
// when his ESPN stats show a redshirt season (a season since he enrolled with 1-4 games, or more college seasons than
// his class): approximate, as in cfb-players.js. s26 / s25: his 2026 (to date) and 2025 FBS lines, summed from ESPN's
// box scores (g = ESPN games played; ff = ESPN's season feed). skin: the median skin-coloured pixel of his ESPN
// headshot's face box (null without a photo).
//
// ── Grade scale (the NFL 0-11 scale, read against college players, as data/cfb-players.js) ────────────────────
//   0 F · 1 D · 2 C- · 3 C · 4 C+ · 5 B- · 6 B · 7 B+ · 8 A- · 9 A · 10 A+ · 11 S
//   Checked on the output (average of the nine traits, Size included; median college OVR):
{{DIST}}
//   (the QB/WR/RB file, same scale: P4 starters 6.3-6.8, G6 5.5-5.9, backups 5.0-5.4). A tackle's trait average
//   runs below an edge's by design: the NFL file's tackles average 5.9 across their traits and its edges 7.2 (bend,
//   speed, get-off and finesse are edge traits), and calcOVRDL weights those heavily; tackles carry Power, Strength and
//   Block Shed instead. Average trait by spot:
{{TRAITS}}
//   College OVR (calcOVRDL through utils/cfbOvr.js collegeOVR) over all rows: {{OVR}}.
//   The top 15 by OVR:
{{TOP}}
//   The top of the board, read against the consensus (2026-11-25 check). A 99 is for a consensus top-3 college lineman.
//   Colin Simmons (99) is the one: Kiper's No. 5 overall and top edge, PFF's top edge, a unanimous CBS midseason
//   All-American, 10.5 sacks and 16 TFL in 8 games (PFF pass rush 87.6) against an SEC schedule. Will Heldt (98) has
//   the next case: PFF 90.5 overall (10th of 877 edges), pass rush 90.0, 37 pressures, 14 TFL in the ACC, first-round
//   in USA Today's (No. 18) and CBS's (No. 25) mocks. Clev Lubin (PFF 84.5, 32nd; No. 47 on the consensus board) and
//   Leroy Harris III (PFF 91.6, 3rd, run defense 2nd; on no board or All-America list found) are 95s, not 99s.
//   Before this check Heldt, Lubin and Harris sat at 99 over Simmons (97). Two causes, both fixed in the model, not by
//   hand: rates were per game, so the busiest ends (Lubin 54 snaps a game, Harris 50) got credit for volume (step 2,
//   now per snap); and a PFF grade counted in full at 331 snaps, so Simmons's run-defense grade on 115 run snaps
//   (68.0) pulled him down like a full season's (step 6, now weighted by each grade's own snaps).
//
// ── How a grade is made ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// 1. Stats: ESPN box scores of every FBS game, 2026 (weight 1.0 a game), 2025 (0.6) and 2024 (0.35): tackles, solo,
//    sacks, TFL, QB hurries, passes defended (at the line, batted balls), fumbles recovered; forced fumbles and games
//    played from ESPN's season feed. Career games add 2022-23 from the feed.
// 2. Rates per snap for 2026: PFF's 2026 snap count / 40 (a starter's median snaps a game) stands in for his 2026
//    games, so a 55-snap-a-game end's tackles and TFL don't read as quality a 40-snap rusher lacks (2024-25 have no
//    snap counts and stay per game). Rates shrunk toward a prior by slot: rate = (count + 5 x prior) / (games + 5), prior = the median rate of
//    the qualified men at his spot (edges, tackles) x 1.0 for EDGE1 and DT1, 0.85 for EDGE2, 0.7 for everyone else.
// 3. Z-scores against every qualified lineman (4+ weighted games, about 1,800 men) at his spot: edges against edges,
//    tackles against tackles (a tackle's sack rate is half an edge's: pooled, every tackle would read as a poor rusher;
//    the spot's base grades put the NFL file's edge/tackle gap back). Count rates enter as square roots (sacks are skewed).
// 4. Trait evidence (z-scores; weight = his weight z at his spot):
//      getOff: sacks/game .4, hurries/game .3, TFL/game .3
//      bend: (sacks + hurries)/game .7, sacks/game .3 (a tackle's bend is 45% of that: inside it is mostly his prior)
//      finesseMoves: sacks .45, hurries .35, lighter frame .2
//      powerMoves: sacks .4, TFL .3, weight .3
//      strength: weight .55, TFL .3, tackles .15 (tackles: weight .5, TFL .25, tackles .25)
//      blockShed: tackles/game .45, TFL/game .35, solo share .2
//      playRecognition: TFL .3, passes defended (batted balls) .2, forced + recovered fumbles .2, career games .3
//      speed: frame (lighter is faster) .75, sacks .25 (no verified 40 or track times were found for these men)
//    Each mix is re-standardized at his spot.
// 5. HIS LEVEL (the tight-end file's step): 0.35 sacks, 0.25 hurries, 0.25 TFL, 0.15 tackles a game (z at his spot),
//    re-standardized, + 0.25 x the z-score of the average FPI offensive efficiency of the 2026 opponents he played
//    (FCS = 12; the offense pools' step 4 turned around), + 0.15 for a Power 4 team (Notre Dame included), - 0.15 otherwise.
// 6. PFF check: PFF's 2026 season grades for every man it charts, from its public player pages (pass-rush and run-defense
//    grades, pressures, snaps) and team grade pages (overall grade and snaps for every lineman). Box scores can't see
//    pass-rush wins that don't end in a sack, double teams or run fits; PFF grades every snap. His pass-rush and
//    run-defense grades become z-scores among the graded men at his spot (100+ snaps), mapped onto the box-score level
//    of the same men, then: pass level = box + wPass x (PFF pass - box), run level = box + wRun x (PFF run - box).
//    Each grade is weighted by its own sample: wPass = c x min(1, pass-rush snaps / 220), wRun = c x min(1, run-defense
//    snaps / 200) (a starter's medians), c = 0.55 at edge and 0.7 at tackle (a tackle's box score sees the least of
//    his work). A run grade built on 115 run snaps moves a man about half as far as a full season's.
//    The schedule and Power 4 terms are added after, since PFF grades are not opponent-adjusted.
// 7. A trait = 0.62 x level + 0.5 x (that trait's evidence minus the average of his eight): the level decides how good
//    he is, the evidence what he is good at. Pass traits (get-off, bend, finesse, power) use the pass level, run traits
//    (strength, block shed, recognition) the run level, speed the box-score level.
// 8. grade = base + 1.05 x 2.0 x z (x 0.85 below average) + 0.35 x max(0, z - 1)^2, rounded, 0-11; 11 (S) needs z >= 2.7.
//    base = the grade of the average qualified man at his spot (backups included), shaped like the NFL file:
//      edge   getOff 5.4 speed 5.9 power 4.8 finesse 5.2 strength 5.0 recognition 4.7 bend 5.2 shed 4.6
//      tackle getOff 3.8 speed 3.0 power 5.5 finesse 3.1 strength 6.2 recognition 4.9 bend 2.4 shed 5.1
// 9. Size is physical, from ESPN height and weight, on the NFL file's own formula against his spot (data/dls.js
//    dlSizeGrade: 85% weight, 15% height; edge 233-280 lb / 73-78 in, tackle 257-345 lb / 72-78 in), off the curve.
// ovr: utils/simulation.js calcOVRDL (DL_ATTR_WEIGHT), then utils/cfbOvr.js collegeOVR, the build's own number.
//
// ── Hand checks (2026-11-25) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Every Power 4 EDGE1 / DT1 and every Group of 6 man in the formula's top 40 was checked against PFF's 2026 season
// grades and pressures (every row: step 6), PFF's article charts (Weeks 1-9 edge grades, Weeks 1-12 pass-rush win rate
// and run-stop rate), the 2027 draft boards (Kiper's mid-November board, Jordan Reid's top 50, PFF's early edge and
// interior rankings, Ourlads' and AtoZ's edge previews), the 2026 midseason All-America teams (CBS, On3, Athlon, CFN),
// the Walter Camp preseason team, the Nagurski finalists and the injury news. Most of what the boards and teams say
// the PFF step had already put in (the board names sit in the top 25, the national sack leaders in the top 60). Hand changes
// (formula -> hand), each with its reason:
{{HAND}}
//
// ── Sources ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
//  ESPN box scores (site.api.espn.com .../college-football/summary), team schedules and rosters, season feed
//  (site.web.api.espn.com .../statistics/byathlete), FPI 2026 (data/cfb-teams.js offEff)
//  PFF: public player pages (www.pff.com/ncaa/players/...), team grade pages (www.pff.com/grades/ncaa/teams/...), and
//  articles (Weeks 1-9 edge grades, Weeks 1-12 pass-rush win rates, preseason and draft rankings). Nothing from Wikipedia.
